name: Perceptual Speed
definition: The ability to quickly and accurately compare similarities and differences among sets of letters, numbers, objects, pictures, or patterns. The things to be compared may be presented at the same time or one after the other. This ability also includes comparing a presented object with a remembered object.

benchmark.name: HPatches
benchmark.metric: mean average precision (mAP, %) on HPatches patch verification
benchmark.human_reference: General adult workforce doing visual same/different comparison tasks (perceptual-speed style work such as inspection or clerical/visual matching)

benchmark.name: NLVR2
benchmark.metric: accuracy (%) on NLVR2 public test set (test-P)
benchmark.human_reference: General adult population (typical workers who visually compare pictures or object sets against a description)

benchmark.name: BLINK
benchmark.metric: accuracy (%) on the BLINK validation set, multiple choice
benchmark.human_reference: General adult workforce (people doing routine visual comparison and matching at work: inspection, clerical checking, data verification)

benchmark.name: BLINK
benchmark.human_reference: General adult population (Perceptual Speed is a basic perceptual-comparison ability used across ordinary work settings)

benchmark.name: BLINK
benchmark.human_reference: General adult population. Perceptual speed and visual comparison are basic abilities used across many jobs, and BLINK tasks were designed to be solvable by ordinary humans 'within a blink'.
